rec.R1.t: Pre-position brigades and equipment; review the contingency plan
rec.R1.d: Critical class forecast for next month.
rec.R2.t: Preventive alert to the population and awareness campaign

rec.R3.t: Coordinate with FUNAI and community leaders; prioritize firebreaks around the land
rec.R3.d: Critical class forecast on indigenous land in one of the three months.
rec.R4.t: Step up inspections; suspend controlled-burn permits

rec.R5.t: Schedule extra crews for the forecast peak month

rec.R6.d: Historically recurrent area (V ≥ 0.75) with a normal forecast.
rec.R7.t: Request state/federal support; consider temporary firefighters
rec.R7.d: At least 20 % of the municipality's cells with a critical forecast.

ia.label: Assistant
ia.title: Ask about the area or the cell
ia.s1: Why is this cell a priority?
ia.input: Ask about this area or the selected cell…
ia.note: Only cites numbers from the loaded context. It explains; it does not decide.
met.label: Transparency
met.title: How forecast and priority are computed
met.top: Precision in the 10 % most-alerted vs. base rate
met.top_r: the wider the gap, the more useful
met.not_t: It is not the probability of an individual fire, nor spread, burned area or severity. The PPI ranks attention; it is not a probability of disaster. Recommendations support the manager and are accepted or ignored by a person. The three-month forecast has little skill over climatology.
met.ipp_n: N forecast: rank of forecast fire (weight 0.75) and of forecast ÷ median (0.25), among cells with forecast fire only; no fire keeps N at the floor.
met.ipp_v: V history: rank of the cell's cumulative 2003–2025 activity.
met.ipp_e: E exposure: population of the cell itself (GHSL 2025, ~1 km), floor 0.8 on indigenous land.
met.cuts: M+{h} cuts (among cells with forecast fire): medium ≥ {m} · high ≥ {a} · top ≥ {c}, and top requires fire above normal
